label: Bubalornis_albirostris
summary: The white-billed buffalo weaver (Bubalornis albirostris) is a resident breeding bird species in most of Africa south of the Sahara Desert. This common weaver occurs in open country, especially cultivation and scrub. It is a communal breeder, building massive untidy stick nests in tree colonies, each of which may have several spherical woven nests within.

appearance.colors: The white-billed buffalo weaver (Bubalornis albirostris) is a resident breeding bird species in most of Africa south of the Sahara Desert. The white-billed buffalo weaver is large and stocky, commonly measuring 23 to 24 centimeters.
appearance.wings: The adult is mainly black with white flecking on the back and wings.
